subject: chemistry
title: Percentage yield
key_idea: (Separate chemistry) The yield is the mass of product actually made. The percentage yield compares it with the maximum theoretical mass. It is nearly always less than 100%, because reactions are incomplete, product is lost, or side reactions happen.

sections.heading: Why the yield is less than 100%

blocks.text: (Separate chemistry) No atoms are lost in a reaction, but you rarely collect all of the product you calculate. This section covers the reasons.

items.meaning: The mass of product actually made in the experiment.
The maximum mass of product that could be made, calculated from the balanced equation.
The actual yield as a percentage of the theoretical yield.

blocks.text: There are three main reasons for a percentage yield below 100%.

items: **Incomplete reaction.** The reaction may not go to completion, because it is reversible or has not been left long enough. Some reactant is left over.
**Losses.** Some product is lost when it is separated from the mixture, such as in filtering, transferring or purifying, or it escapes from the apparatus.
**Side reactions.** Some of the reactants react in ways different to the expected reaction.
Actual yield is what you make. Theoretical yield is the maximum possible.
Reasons for a low yield: incomplete reaction, losses, side reactions.
No atoms are lost. The yield is lower because product is not collected.

blocks.text: Divide the actual yield by the theoretical yield. Both must be in the same unit.

blocks.label: Percentage yield
blocks.formula: percentage yield = (mass of product actually made ÷ maximum theoretical mass of product) × 100
where: Both masses in the same unit, such as g or tonnes.

items.text: 60.0 kg of aluminium oxide gives a maximum of 31.8 kg of aluminium. Only 28.4 kg is made.

diagram.alt: Practise calculating a percentage yield from an actual mass and a theoretical mass.
diagram.question: The maximum theoretical mass of a salt is 12.5 g. A student makes **{a} g** of the salt. Calculate the percentage yield.
working: Percentage yield = actual yield ÷ theoretical yield × 100

blocks.text: Finding the theoretical yield (Higher tier for AQA)

items.text: I₂ : ZnI₂ = 1 : 1, so 0.025 mol of ZnI₂.

items: Actual yield = percentage yield ÷ 100 × theoretical yield. A factory predicts 60 tonnes at 78% yield: 78 ÷ 100 × 60 = 46.8 tonnes.
Theoretical yield = actual yield × 100 ÷ percentage yield. For 4.22 g made at 80%: 4.22 × 100 ÷ 80 = 5.275 g.
Find the theoretical mass from the equation using moles.
Rearrange to find the actual or theoretical yield.

checks.q: State two reasons why the actual yield of a reaction is less than the theoretical yield.
checks.a: Any two from: some reactant is left unreacted (incomplete reaction); some product is lost during separation or purification; side reactions occur.

checks.q: A student predicts 7.6 g of iron sulfate but makes 5.4 g. Calculate the percentage yield to 1 decimal place.
The theoretical mass of a salt is 12.5 g and the percentage yield is 92.8%. Calculate the mass actually produced.

worked_example.question:
A student used 6.35 g of iodine in the reaction. 6.29 g of zinc iodide was produced.

The equation for the reaction is:

Zn + I₂ → ZnI₂

Relative formula masses (Mr): I₂ = 254, ZnI₂ = 319

Calculate the percentage yield of zinc iodide.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the moles, the theoretical mass, the expression, the value and the rounding.

worked_example.question:
Titanium can be extracted from titanium oxide, TiO₂, by reaction with magnesium.

100 tonnes of titanium oxide was heated with magnesium.

The titanium formed in the reaction was separated and purified.

The mass of titanium was then determined. The results were:

mass of titanium oxide: 100.00 tonnes
mass of titanium produced: 45.26 tonnes
theoretical mass of titanium formed: 60.00 tonnes

Calculate the percentage yield of titanium in this process.

percentage yield = (actual yield ÷ theoretical yield) × 100

Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
worked_example.tip: Use the actual yield (45.26) and the theoretical yield (60.00). The mass of titanium oxide is not used.

worked_example.question:
A student neutralises dilute sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, with ammonia, NH₃, to make ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄.

This is the equation for the reaction.

H₂SO₄ + 2NH₃ → (NH₄)₂SO₄

The student makes 4.22 g of ammonium sulfate. The percentage yield is 80%.

Calculate the mass of sulfuric acid the student used in the reaction.

Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): H = 1.0, N = 14.0, O = 16.0, S = 32.1
answer_points: Mr of H₂SO₄ = 98.1 and Mr of (NH₄)₂SO₄ = 132.1 (1)
worked_example.tip: The ratio of H₂SO₄ to (NH₄)₂SO₄ is 1 : 1, so the Mr values scale the mass directly.

worked_example.question:
Iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, in iron ore is converted to iron when it reacts with carbon monoxide in a blast furnace.

Calculate the percentage by mass of iron in iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃.
answer_points: Mass of iron in one formula unit = 2 × 56 = 112
worked_example.tip: (Supplement) One mark for the Mr and one mark for the percentage.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Percentage purity compares the mass of the pure substance with the mass of the whole sample.

blocks.label: Percentage purity
blocks.formula: percentage purity = (mass of pure substance ÷ mass of impure sample) × 100
where: Both masses in the same unit, such as g.

items.lead: Find the mass of pure substance.
items.text: A 2.50 g sample of impure copper(II) sulfate contains 2.00 g of pure copper(II) sulfate.

items: A purity below 100% means impurities are present.
Rearrange to find the pure mass: pure mass = purity ÷ 100 × sample mass. A 10.0 g sample that is 80% pure contains 8.0 g of the substance.

worked_example.question:
Ethanol is made by the fermentation of glucose.

A mixture containing 500 mol of glucose is fermented. A mass of 5750 g of ethanol is obtained.

Calculate the percentage yield.

[for ethanol, Mr = 46]
answer_points: Fermentation: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂, so 500 mol of glucose gives 500 × 2 = 1000 mol of ethanol
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. The answer can also be found by comparing the moles: 125 ÷ 1000 × 100.
